battle.name: 玄武門事變
battle.brief: 西元626年武德九年六月初四，李世民在長安玄武門伏擊太子李建成、齊王李元吉，尉遲敬德斬元吉，三日後逼李淵退位。卡面亞述長弓屬兩河流域亞述弓兵裝備，與本役相隔逾千年，不在現場；此役實戰以唐制步弩、直臂弓與佩刀、馬槊近身格鬥為主。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 玄武門事變沒有跨國交戰，交戰雙方同屬唐帝國皇室內部：一方是太子李建成為首的東宮集團，另一方是秦王李世民為首的西府集團，兵鋒只在長安皇城北門內外相接。按《舊唐書》與《資治通鑑》的記法，東宮一方有左率府、詹事府、典膳坊等屬官領兵，李建成以太子身份統率東宮武備，其部曲宿於皇城玄武門東側一帶，齊王李元吉在齊王府另置僚屬，並以河南、山東的舊部與地方人脈為外援。西府一方則以秦王府的將士與府兵為骨幹，長孫無忌、房玄齡、杜如晦、裴矩等參贊謀劃，尉遲敬德、秦叔寶、程知節、段志玄、劉師立、公孫武達、侯君集等將領領甲士隨行；關鍵在於玄武門宿衛的替換，以及皇城禁軍中可用之兵的實際傾向。指揮系統上，李淵以皇帝身份總攬禁軍與北衙六軍，但無法即時調動玄武門一線的實際指揮者；事變當日，玄武門守將常何所部在門道關鍵位置上仍按太子的命令站著，而李世民一方則藉宿衛交班的名義在同一位置完成佈防。雙方同樣受制於皇城門道與城樓的狹窄地形，戰鬥規模有限而時間極短，勝負全在封鎖與突然性。
countriesEn: The Xuanwu Gate Incident was not a war between states. Both sides belonged to the imperial house of the Tang, and their weapons met inside the northern gate of the Chang'an imperial city. On one side stood the Eastern Palace party of Crown Prince Li Jiancheng, whose bureaus — the Left Command Guard, the Office of Palace Affairs and the Palace Food Service — supplied the officers and men, and whose own guard quarters lay to the east of the Xuanwu Gate; Prince of Qi Li Yuanji kept a separate staff in his own princely residence and drew on his following in Henan and in Shandong as a second pillar of support. On the other side stood the West Depot party of Prince of Qin Li Shimin, built on the household troops and regional soldiers of the Qin residence, with Changsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui and Pei Ju shaping the plan and the officers Wei Chigong (Yuchi Jingde), Qin Shubao, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, Liu Shili, Gongsun Wuda and Hou Junji leading armoured men into the gate. The decisive element was the substitution of the gate garrison and the real alignment of the imperial guards of the imperial city. As emperor, Li Yuan held the overall command of the palace guards and the Northern Gate Army, yet he could not reach the officer who actually commanded the Xuanwu Gate line on that morning. The commander of the gate garrison, Chang He, still stood where the crown prince's orders placed him, while Li Shimin's side had already completed its deployment in the same position under the pretext of a routine change of watch. Both parties were equally confined by the narrow gate tunnel, the flanking gate towers and the raised causeways of the imperial city. The fighting was therefore narrow in frontage and extremely short in duration, and the outcome was decided entirely by blockage and surprise.
people: 事件的關鍵人物幾乎全部集中在唐高祖李淵的三個兒子與一批北衙將領身上。李世民時年二十八歲，任尚書令、秦王，兵權在握，玄武門一役由他一手策劃並親自指揮伏擊；傳世記載稱他在門內追射太子李建成，一箭中其身，隨即又被齊王李元吉的馬槊刺中右腿，股血流滿靴，猶自不退。太子李建成居儲位而性柔緩，屢次在父親面前與李世民交鋒，軍功才具皆遜於弟；齊王李元吉曾任太尉、在地方經營州縣多年，善於收買將領，與建成結盟，是事變中直接持械相攻者。尉遲敬德為事變中斬元吉者，持單鞭突入重圍，殺散東宮與齊王府甲士；秦叔寶與程知節各引兵分守玄武門兩側通道；常何身為玄武門宿衛首長，其臨陣傾向直接決定門道的控制權。幕後有裴矩屢勸世民先行下手，以關中與關東形勢相逼，促其速斷；房玄齡、杜如晦力主果斷誅除兄弟以絕後患，認為建成一旦入宮告變，突擊便不再可能。魏徵時為建成洗馬，事變後降而為太宗所用，成為貞觀之治的重要謀臣。李淵在事變當日被驚起於內廷，事後被迫追認既成事實，於是先立太子，再傳帝位。
peopleEn: Almost every decisive person in the incident was either one of the three sons of Emperor Gaozu Li Yuan or one of the palace officers who served them. Li Shimin was twenty-eight years old, holding the post of President of the Department of State Affairs and the title Prince of Qin, with military command in his hands; he planned the Xuanwu Gate operation and led the ambush himself. The transmitted accounts say that he pursued the crown prince inside the gate and shot Li Jiancheng in the body, and was then struck in the right thigh by the lance of Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, blood running down his boot, yet he refused to withdraw. Li Jiancheng, who occupied the position of crown prince, was gentle and slow in temperament, repeatedly collided with Li Shimin in front of their father, and was inferior to him in both merit and ability. Li Yuanji had served as Commandant of the Imperial Guards, governed prefectures and counties for years in the provinces, was skilled at buying the loyalty of officers, and had allied himself with Jiancheng; he was the one who fought with weapons in the incident itself. Wei Chigong, known as Yuchi Jingde, was the man who cut down Li Yuanji; he pushed into the melee with his single whalebone staff and cut down the men of the Eastern Palace and of the Qi residence. Qin Shubao and Cheng Zhijie each led a detachment to hold the two passages on either side of the gate. Chang He, commander of the Xuanwu Gate garrison, decided by his behaviour on the day who would hold the gate passage. Behind the scenes, Pei Ju repeatedly urged Li Shimin to strike first, arguing from the situation in Guanzhong and in the east that he must act without delay. Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui insisted on killing the brothers at once to end the danger, holding that once Jiancheng entered the palace to accuse him the surprise attack would never be possible again. Wei Zheng was then the literary attendant of the crown prince; after the incident he submitted to Li Shimin and became an important adviser of the Zhenguan reign. Li Yuan was roused from the inner palace that morning, and afterwards had little choice but to ratify accomplished fact, first appointing the new crown prince and later yielding the throne.
kits: 卡面那件亞述長弓製作於公元前七百年前後，是兩河流域亞述王國的弓兵裝備，木胎覆皮或嵌骨、以金屬箍加固，靠射手拉弦與弓臂回彈提供推力；它與唐初長安的戰陣相隔一千三百多年，並未出現在中國的軍備序列中，此役現場的兵器屬另一套體系。玄武門一役真正投入的裝備主要有三類。其一是投射類：唐制弩機，包括擘張弩、臂弩與小型腰弩，配竹木或角木之弩，箭鏃用鋼或鐵，箭桿用木；以及射手手持的直臂弓（唐人稱胡弓），軍中分步射與馬射，弓手陣列前用大盾與拒馬護衛。其二是近戰類：佩刀（橫刀、格門刀）、長柄馬槊、方天畫戟與長槊；玄武門門道狹窄，騎兵無法展開，馬槊與長刀成為主要格鬥兵器，李世民的腿傷與李建成、元吉的致命傷皆出於此類。其三是防護與披具：頭戴兜鍪，身穿明光鎧與札甲，內襯綿甲，配護臂護腿，另有長柄大盾與小型手盾。輔助器材包括封門用的木柵、拒馬槓、繩索、火把與號角，玄武門的門扇與門鎖本身也是戰具。因無攻城與野戰，此役不涉雲梯、撞車與投石車，只有宮門道內短距離的遭遇式格鬥。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card was made around 700 BC and was the standard bow of the Assyrian armies of Mesopotamia: a wooden core faced with hide or bone, reinforced with metal bands, powered by the draw of the archer and the rebound of the limbs. It is more than thirteen hundred years removed from the fighting at Tang-era Chang'an and never entered the Chinese order of battle, and the weapons actually present in this incident belonged to an entirely different system. Three groups of equipment were really employed at Xuanwu Gate. First, the missile weapons: Tang crossbows, including the draw-heavy crossbow, the arm-powered crossbow and small waist-mounted crossbows, made of bamboo, wood or horn, with steel or iron heads and wooden shafts; together with the straight-limb bows held in the hand, which the Tang called hu bows, the army listing archers separately as foot archers and mounted archers, with large shields and barricades protecting the front of the archer line. Second, the hand-to-hand weapons: the side-sword, both the hengdao and the single-edged pattern, long-handled lances, the fangtian pole-axe and the long ma; because the gate passage was narrow and cavalry could not deploy, the lance and the sword became the principal weapons of the fight, and the wound in Li Shimin's leg as well as the fatal wounds of Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji all came from this class of arm. Third, protection: iron helmets, the bright-plated and lamellar cuirasses, cotton-padded underlayers, arm and leg guards, long-handled shields and smaller hand shields. The auxiliary gear included wooden palisades, spiked barricades, ropes, torches and horns used to seal the gate, and the gate leaves and the lock itself were treated as weapons. Since there was no siege and no field action, no scaling ladders, battering rams or stone-throwers were involved; this was a short, meeting engagement fought inside a palace gate passage.
tactics: 李世民用的是一次典型的門道伏擊，而不是正面交鋒。玄武門是長安皇城北門，位於皇城正北中軸線上，門道狹長，兩側有城樓、宿衛所與內溝，門內通禁軍屯營，門外即入禁苑；再往南約一千五百米上下，經皇城縱深而至宮城南門承天門，承天門內的玄武殿是皇帝日常聽政之所。選在此處有三個好處：一是門道寬度有限，寬處亦不過容數騎並行，騎兵無法展開衝鋒，只能下馬步戰或以少數人擠壓；二是門內外的宿衛可提前以交班輪值的名義替換，誰掌握守門指揮權，誰就掌握作戰的主動；三是玄武門距宮城近，得手後可立刻控制出入通道，切斷太子與齊王向外求援的路徑。部署上，世民先召長孫無忌、尉遲敬德、秦叔寶、程知節等入玄武門內議事，隨後分兵埋伏於門道兩側與城樓之下，命人多帶甲兵、閉門自守；李建成與李元吉各自率東宮與齊王府少數護衛騎馬入門，世民發難，執弓射擊建成，尉遲敬德持單鞭下馬斬元吉，隨即以少量人數驅散並斬殺屯於門東的東宮左率府兵。事後世民不究宿衛之罪，盡收其兵器入庫，並命人把死者首級拋於門外。戰鬥自破曉前動手，至日出後收束，全程不足一刻鐘，靠的不是兵力優勢，而是位置、封鎖與突然性。
tacticsEn: Li Shimin executed a classic ambush in a gate passage rather than a general engagement. The Xuanwu Gate was the north gate of the imperial city of Chang'an, standing on the central axis of the city's northern wall, with a long narrow tunnel, gate towers, guard quarters and a dry ditch on either side; inside lay the camp of the palace guards, and outside lay the imperial park. Running south, through the depth of the imperial city and on to the Chengtian Gate of the palace city some one and a half kilometres away, one reached the Xuanwu Hall where the emperor normally held court. Choosing this spot offered three advantages. First, the gate tunnel was narrow, broad enough at best for a few horsemen abreast, so cavalry could not deploy in a charge and could only fight on foot or press through in small numbers. Second, the guards inside and outside the gate could be substituted beforehand under the pretext of a routine change of watch, and whoever held the command of the gate held the initiative of the battle. Third, the Xuanwu Gate lay close to the palace city, so once it was taken the passages of entry and exit were immediately under control and the crown prince and the prince of Qi were cut off from any route of appeal. In the deployment, Li Shimin first summoned Changsun Wuji, Yuchi Jingde, Qin Shubao and Cheng Zhijie into the gate to confer, and then posted them in ambush along both sides of the passage and beneath the gate towers, ordering more armoured men to be brought and the gates kept shut. Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji entered on horseback each with a few guards from the Eastern Palace and the Qi residence; Li Shimin gave the signal, shot at Jiancheng with his bow, and Yuchi Jingde dismounted with his staff and cut down Yuanji, after which a small number of men drove off and killed the East Guard troops posted east of the gate. Afterwards Li Shimin did not punish the gate garrison for its conduct, took all its weapons into store, and ordered the severed heads of the dead thrown outside the gate. The fighting began before daybreak and was closed up after sunrise; the whole action took less than a quarter of an hour, and it was won not by superior numbers but by position, blockage and surprise.
data: 關於這場事變的具體數字，傳世史料留下的並不多，可確定的部分大致如下。時間點是武德九年六月初四，即西元626年7月2日，時值破曉之前，玄武門之役在日出前後即告結束，歷時不足一刻鐘。當日投入的甲士規模有限，玄武門屯兵與秦王府隨行將士合計應在數百人上下；李建成一方在門東屯有東宮左率府兵力，舊籍記其編制為千餘人，玄武門事變中這支部隊被尉遲敬德等驅散斬首，數十人當場授首，殘部潰散。與之相應，玄武門宿衛為常何所領的屯營人馬，數量同樣在千人量級，關鍵在於其中一部已由世民掌握，門道兩側另有世民親信的甲士伏兵。距離上，玄武門至宮城南門承天門約一千五百米上下，門外北面即入禁苑，其縱深以里計；玄武門置於皇城正北中軸線上，門道寬度有限，寬處亦不過容數騎並行，不足以展開衝鋒陣形。時間上，自事變到李淵立李世民為太子僅隔三日，至武德九年八月李淵傳位、李世民即位並改元貞觀，歷時不足兩個月。傷亡方面，玄武門門道內的當場陣亡與被斬首級以數十計，含建成、元吉及數名東宮、齊王府武官；此後追捕、誅除與流放涉及的官員將佐達數十至百餘人級別，數字多見於《資治通鑑》與《舊唐書》各傳記的零散記載，不宜相加為精確總數。
dataEn: The transmitted record does not preserve many exact figures for this incident, but the following can be stated. The date was the fourth day of the sixth month of Wude, the ninth year, that is 2 July 626, in the hours before daybreak; the action at Xuanwu Gate was closed up around sunrise and lasted less than a quarter of an hour. The number of armoured men engaged was small: the garrison of the gate together with the Qin household men who accompanied Li Shimin probably amounted to several hundred. On Li Jiancheng's side, troops of the Eastern Palace Left Guard were posted east of the gate, the old registers giving that unit a strength of a little over a thousand men; in the incident this body was driven off and cut down by Wei Chigong and the others, several dozen falling on the spot and the rest breaking up. Correspondingly, the garrison of Xuanwu Gate was the picked company under Chang He, also on the order of a thousand men, the decisive point being that a part of it already answered to Li Shimin, with further ambush detachments of his own trusted men posted on both sides of the tunnel. As to distance, the run from Xuanwu Gate south to the Chengtian Gate of the palace city was on the order of one and a half kilometres, and immediately to the north beyond the gate lay the imperial park, whose depth was measured in li; the gate itself stood on the central north-south axis of the imperial city, and its tunnel was so narrow that even at its widest it would admit only a few horsemen abreast, far too little to deploy a charge. In time, only three days separated the incident from Li Yuan's appointment of Li Shimin as crown prince, and it was less than two months more before Li Yuan yielded the throne, Li Shimin took the imperial title and the reign name Zhenguan was proclaimed. On losses, the dead and the severed heads inside the gate passage on the day numbered several dozen, including Li Jiancheng, Li Yuanji and several officers of the Eastern Palace and the Qi residence; the subsequent arrests, executions and banishments of officials and officers ran to the score or hundred, and these figures come in scattered entries in the Zizhi Tongjian and the Old Book of Tang rather than in a single tally, so they should not be added up into a precise total.
cause: 玄武門事變的起因不是外敵入侵，而是唐初帝國最高權力在父子四人與兩批宗室將領之間的失衡。開國之後，李世民在滅隋、平定竇建德與王世充、收復河東與關中的戰爭中居功至偉，被封秦王、拜尚書令，總領兵權，士卒歸心多半向之；李建成以長子居太子位，卻在軍功、才幹與人望上都遜於弟弟，於是與同樣封王的李元吉結盟，藉齊王府在地方經營的州縣與人脈鞏固自身的儲位同盟，李元吉則屢次勸建成盡早除掉世民，並代他在父親面前進言。父親李淵的態度是全部衝突的根源：他既倚重世民的兵，又不能廢掉已立的太子，更偏愛幼子元吉，工於心計地把兄弟之間的矛盾縱容成公開的傾軋。朝政層面，建成一系在京城安插親信於北衙禁軍與京師宿衛，令玄武門等門禁的實際守備落到自己人手上；世民一方的兵權重心則在洛陽與河南道，班師之後久居京師北面的秦府，加上東宮提議調世民出京遠征並削其兵權，均使形勢急轉。裴矩屢勸世民先行下手，以關東與關中形勢相逼，勸他不可坐失其機；房玄齡、杜如晦則力主不可再拖，因為建成一旦入宮告變，玄武門的突擊便不再可能。於是武德九年六月，世民決定先下手。
causeEn: The cause of the Xuanwu Gate Incident was not an invasion from abroad. It was the imbalance of supreme power in the early Tang, spread across a father, his three sons and two groups of princely officers. After the founding of the dynasty, Li Shimin had been by far the most meritorious of the princes in the campaigns that destroyed the Sui, defeated Dou Jiande and Wang Shichong, and recovered Hedong and Guanzhong; he was made Prince of Qin and President of the Department of State Affairs, held the command of the troops, and the soldiers' allegiance leaned towards him. Li Jiancheng, the eldest son, held the position of crown prince, yet in military achievement, ability and popular regard he was his brother's inferior; he therefore allied with Li Yuanji, himself a crowned prince, and used the prefectures and the local connections cultivated by the Qi residence to consolidate the alliance of the two. Yuanji repeatedly urged Jiancheng to remove Shimin early, and spoke for him in front of their father. The attitude of the father, Li Yuan, lay at the root of the whole conflict: he relied on Shimin for his soldiers, yet could not depose a crown prince already installed, and he favoured the youngest son; with great cunning he let the rivalry between the brothers fester into open plotting. At the level of the court, the Jiancheng party planted its own men in the Northern Gate Army and in the metropolitan watch, so that the actual guarding of gates such as Xuanwu Gate passed into the hands of his creatures. The centre of Li Shimin's military power lay meanwhile at Luoyang and in Henan circuit; after the campaigns he had long been established in the Qin residence north of the capital, and the Eastern Palace's proposal to send him on distant service and strip his command sharpened the situation. Pei Ju urged Li Shimin repeatedly to strike first, pressing on him the contrast between the east of the passes and Guanzhong and warning him not to let the moment pass. Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui were for immediate action, holding that once Jiancheng entered the palace to make his accusation, the surprise attack at Xuanwu Gate would never be possible again. In the sixth month of the ninth year of Wude, therefore, Li Shimin decided to strike first.
impact: 玄武門事變直接改寫了唐帝國的皇位歸屬，也改寫了此後數百年中國政治文化的樣貌。短期看，李世民以既成事實逼父退位，殺死太子與齊王，清理兩府屬官而大赦多數舊人，得以在沒有大規模內戰的情況下接掌帝國，避免了第二場隋末式的內爭；一批原屬建成、元吉的人才如魏徵、房玄齡、杜如晦等被吸收入新朝，統治集團因此得以重組而不致斷裂。制度上，貞觀之治在此後二十三年推行均田、租庸調，完善三省與科舉，編纂《唐律疏議》，修《大唐聖教序》與《貞觀政要》，對內減輕賦役、整頓吏治，對外先平東突厥、再滅高昌、威懾東亞，成為漢唐兩個高峰中的高峰之一；貞觀二字此後成為中文世界理想君主的代名詞。長期看，此役示範了一種權力轉移的樣式：以宮門伏擊解決繼承問題，後世唐末與五代、北宋的宮廷變亂多有仿效者，玄武門三字遂成為中文裡改朝換代與宮廷政變的隱語和象徵，歷代史家在論及此役時，評價從此兩極分化：贊者謂其保境安民、止亂速定，貶者斥其骨肉相殘、權臣篡位之始。在東亞，此事亦透過日本遣隋使、遣唐使帶回的見聞被記錄，與隋末唐初的並立局面一同構成當時國際視野中的唐代開局。
impactEn: The Xuanwu Gate Incident changed directly who would hold the Tang throne, and reshaped the shape of Chinese politics and culture for centuries afterwards. In the short term, Li Shimin forced his father to yield, killed the crown prince and the prince of Qi, purged the officers of the two princely residences while pardoning most of the old men, and took over the empire without a large-scale civil war, thereby sparing the dynasty a second contest of the Sui-end kind. Talented men who had belonged to Jiancheng and Yuanji — Wei Zheng, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui and others — were drawn into the new court, so that the governing group could be reconstituted rather than broken. Institutionally, the Zhenguan reign that followed pushed forward the equal-field system and the grain, labour and silk levies, completed the three departments and the examination system, compiled the Tang Code with Commentary, wrote the Great Tang Proclamation on the Sacred Teachings and the Record of Good Government of the Zhenguan Era, lightened the tax burden and reformed the officials at home, and abroad first broke the Eastern Turks and then destroyed Gaochang, becoming the high peak within the two high peaks of Han and Tang. The two characters Zhenguan thereafter stood as a synonym for the ideal ruler in the Chinese world. In the longer run the incident demonstrated a mode of transferring power: solving the question of succession by an ambush at a palace gate. Many later palace coups in the late Tang, the Five Dynasties and the Northern Song followed that pattern, and the three characters Xuanwu Gate became in Chinese a coded synonym for dynastic turnover and palace revolution. From then on the judgements of historians split in two: those who praise the act say it preserved the realm and settled the disorder quickly; those who condemn it call it the beginning of fratricide and of the usurpation of power by a minister. In East Asia too, the incident was recorded through accounts carried back by the Japanese envoys to Sui and to Tang, and together with the stand-off of the Sui-end and early Tang it formed, in the international view of the time, the opening chapter of the Tang.
result: 玄武門事變的結果在當日便已分曉。太子李建成、齊王李元吉死於門下，太宗李世民隨即控制玄武門與皇城出入，斬東宮、齊王府武官首級拋於門外，解散兩府部眾，宮中宿衛由北衙將領與世民親信重新占位。李淵在武德殿見李世民，責其構釁，終究被迫追認事實，先立李世民為皇太子，繼而於同年八月傳位，李世民即位，改元貞觀，成為唐太宗。原太子府與齊王府的屬官多被貶黜流放，數十名骨幹被誅，餘者赦免；玄武門值守有功的常何事後被貶為潭州都督，以示朝廷對參與政變者的冷待，太宗本人則逐步清洗北衙禁軍高層，確立由將領與宮禁共同拱衛皇室的格局。此役之後，唐朝的外部對手才真正浮出水面：突厥於同一年再度南下，太宗次年遣兵東擊，於陰山破之，貞觀之治的武功篇由此起筆。一場不到一刻鐘的宮門伏擊，結束了李唐開國以來最危險的內部權力危機，換來的是一個延續近三百年的王朝框架。
resultEn: The outcome of the Xuanwu Gate Incident was settled on the day itself. The crown prince Li Jiancheng and the prince of Qi Li Yuanji were killed at the gate, and Taizong Li Shimin immediately took control of Xuanwu Gate and of the entrances to the imperial city; the heads of officers of the Eastern Palace and the Qi residence were cut off and thrown outside the gate, the two parties' contingents were dispersed, and the palace guard posts were refilled by officers of the Northern Gate Army and by Li Shimin's own trusted men. Li Yuan received Li Shimin in the Wude Hall, blamed him for raising the disturbance, and in the end had no choice but to ratify accomplished fact: he first made Li Shimin crown prince, and then in the eighth month of the same year yielded the throne. Li Shimin took the imperial title, proclaimed the reign name Zhenguan, and became Emperor Taizong. The officers of the former crown prince's and prince of Qi's offices were mostly demoted and banished, several dozen of the leading men were executed, and the rest were pardoned. Chang He, who had held the gate on the day, was afterwards demoted to military governor of Tanzhou, a mark of the court's coldness towards those who had taken part in the coup, while Taizong himself gradually purged the senior ranks of the Northern Gate Army and established a system in which the emperor was guarded jointly by the officers and the palace watch. Only after this did the external enemies of the Tang come fully into view: the Turks invaded again in the same year, and the following year Taizong sent troops east and broke them at Mount Yin, opening the martial chapter of the Zhenguan reign. A palace-gate ambush of less than a quarter of an hour ended the most dangerous internal crisis of power since the founding of the Tang, and in exchange left behind the framework of a dynasty that would run for close to three hundred years.
